events.title: Neolithic Settlements
events.description: Çatalhöyük in central Anatolia was one of world's earliest urban settlements, housing up to 10,000 people. This Neolithic city featured mud-brick houses, vibrant murals and sophisticated culture. Çatalhöyük represents early stages of urbanization and agricultural revolution.

events.title: Rise of Hittite Empire
events.description: Indo-European Hittites established an empire in central Anatolia, capital at Hattusa. Hittites were among the first to master iron smelting, possessing powerful chariot forces. Hittite cuneiform recorded rich historical and legal documents.

events.title: Battle of Kadesh
events.description: Hittite King Muwatalli II fought Egyptian Pharaoh Ramesses II at Kadesh (modern Syria). This was one of largest chariot battles in ancient history. Battle ended inconclusively, but led to world's first recorded peace treaty between Hittites and Egypt.

events.title: Sea Peoples Invasion
events.description: Mysterious Sea Peoples attacked eastern Mediterranean, destroying Hittite Empire and many Bronze Age civilizations. Anatolia entered dark age, population centers collapsed. This period marked end of Bronze Age and transition to Iron Age.

events.title: Kingdom of Phrygia
events.description: Phrygian Kingdom rose in central Anatolia, legendary King Midas ruled here. Phrygians made significant contributions to music and metalworking. Their capital Gordium was famous for Gordian Knot legend.

events.title: Lydian Kingdom and Invention of Coinage
events.description: Lydian Kingdom in western Anatolia invented world's first metal coinage. Wealthy King Croesus made Lydia extremely prosperous. Lydian capital Sardis became important commercial center.

events.title: Persian Conquest of Anatolia
events.description: Persian King Cyrus the Great conquered Lydian Kingdom, Anatolia became part of Achaemenid Persian Empire. Persians established satrapy system, Greek cities on coast rebelled multiple times.

events.title: Alexander Conquers Anatolia
events.description: Alexander the Great crossed Hellespont, defeated Persians at Battle of Granicus. Alexander's conquest brought Hellenistic culture to Anatolia, founded many Greek cities. Anatolia became bridge between Greek and Eastern civilizations.

events.title: Roman Annexation of Asia Minor
events.description: Last Attalid king of Pergamon bequeathed kingdom to Rome, Anatolia became Roman province of Asia. Roman rule brought peace and prosperity, many magnificent cities built. Anatolia became one of richest regions of Roman Empire.

events.title: Spread of Christianity in Anatolia
events.description: Apostle Paul preached in Anatolia, establishing many early Christian communities. Seven Churches of Asia mentioned in Book of Revelation were all in Anatolia. Anatolia became important center of early Christianity.

events.title: Council of Nicaea
events.description: First Ecumenical Council held at Nicaea (Iznik) in Anatolia, convened by Emperor Constantine. Council formulated Nicene Creed, defining orthodox Christian doctrine on nature of Christ. This was watershed moment in Christian theology.

events.title: Founding of Constantinople
events.description: Constantine the Great moved the Roman capital from Rome to Byzantium, renaming it Constantinople (present-day Istanbul). This 'New Rome' at the crossroads of Europe and Asia had superior strategic position. Constantinople served as the Eastern Roman (Byzantine) Empire's capital for a millennium.

events.title: Division of Roman Empire
events.description: After Emperor Theodosius I's death, Roman Empire permanently split into Western and Eastern (Byzantine) empires. Constantinople became capital of Eastern Roman Empire. Byzantine Empire preserved Greek-Roman culture and Christian tradition for another thousand years.

events.title: Reign of Justinian the Great
events.description: Emperor Justinian I reconquered much of Western Roman territory, including North Africa and Italy. He codified Roman law (Justinian Code), built Hagia Sophia. Justinian's reign represented Byzantine Empire's golden age.

events.title: Hagia Sophia Completed
events.description: Justinian's Hagia Sophia was completed in Constantinople. This magnificent church featured an enormous dome, the pinnacle of Byzantine architecture. For nearly a millennium it remained Christendom's largest church.

events.title: Arab Conquest Attempts
events.description: Expanding Arab Caliphate launched multiple sieges of Constantinople but Byzantine Empire successfully resisted. Greek fire (secret Byzantine weapon) played key role in defense. Byzantium preserved Christianity in eastern Mediterranean.

events.title: Battle of Manzikert
events.description: Seljuk Turks defeated Byzantines at Manzikert, capturing Emperor Romanos IV. This catastrophic defeat opened Anatolia's heartland to Turkic migration at scale. This battle changed Anatolia's ethnic composition.

events.title: Establishment of Sultanate of Rum
events.description: Seljuk Turks established Sultanate of Rum (Rome) in Anatolia, capital at Konya. This Turkish state blended Persian-Islamic culture with Byzantine traditions. Sultanate of Rum became important center of Turkish-Islamic civilization.

events.title: Fourth Crusade Sacks Constantinople
events.description: Fourth Crusade diverted to sack Constantinople, greatly weakening Byzantine Empire. Crusaders established Latin Empire. Though Byzantines recaptured city in 1261, empire never fully recovered. This catastrophe made Ottoman conquest easier.

events.title: Mongol Invasion of Anatolia
events.description: Mongol armies defeated Sultanate of Rum, Anatolia fell under Mongol Ilkhanate's sphere of influence. Seljuk state weakened, fragmenting into many small beyliks. Mongol destruction created power vacuum filled by Ottomans.

events.title: Ottoman Empire Founded
events.description: Osman I established an independent principality in northwestern Anatolia, the Ottoman Empire's beginning. Osman and successors gradually expanded, conquering Byzantine territory. The Ottomans became one of the world's most powerful and enduring empires.

events.title: Battle of Ankara
events.description: Timur (Tamerlane) defeated Ottoman Sultan Bayezid I at Ankara, temporarily halting Ottoman expansion. Bayezid was captured, dying in captivity. Ottoman princes fought for throne in interregnum period. But Ottomans recovered and resumed expansion.

events.title: Conquest of Constantinople
events.description: 21-year-old Mehmed II (the Conqueror) led Ottoman forces in a 53-day siege capturing Constantinople, ending the Byzantine Empire. This historic event marked the Middle Ages' end. Constantinople was renamed Istanbul, becoming the Ottoman capital. Hagia Sophia was converted into a mosque.

events.title: Battle of Chaldiran
events.description: Sultan Selim I defeated Persian Safavid Empire at Chaldiran, Ottoman firearms proved decisive advantage. Ottomans established themselves as dominant Sunni power against Shi'a Persia. This battle defined Ottoman-Persian border for centuries.

events.title: Conquest of Mamluk Sultanate
events.description: Selim I conquered Mamluk Sultanate, annexing Egypt, Syria and Hejaz (including holy cities Mecca and Medina). Ottoman sultans claimed title of Caliph, becoming protectors of Islam's holiest sites. This made Ottomans undisputed leaders of Islamic world.

events.title: Reign of Suleiman the Magnificent
events.description: Under Suleiman I (the Lawgiver), the Ottoman Empire reached its zenith. He conquered Belgrade, Rhodes, Hungary, and Iraq. Suleiman reformed laws, patronized architecture and arts. Architect Sinan built masterpieces like Süleymaniye Mosque.

events.title: Battle of Lepanto
events.description: Holy League's fleet defeated Ottoman navy at Lepanto, halting Ottoman naval expansion in Mediterranean. Though Ottomans quickly rebuilt fleet, this marked end of Ottoman maritime dominance.

events.title: Second Siege of Vienna
events.description: Ottoman forces again besieged Vienna but were defeated by Polish King Sobieski's relief army. This defeat was a turning point in Ottoman decline. Subsequently, the Holy League counterattacked, Ottomans lost vast European territory.

events.title: Treaty of Karlowitz
events.description: Ottomans signed Treaty of Karlowitz, first major territorial concession to European powers. Ottomans lost Hungary and Transylvania. This treaty marked beginning of Ottoman territorial decline.

events.title: Tulip Era
events.description: Ottoman Empire experienced brief cultural and artistic renaissance called Tulip Era. Tulips were cultivated, Western influences increased. But this luxury era ended with Patrona Halil rebellion.

events.title: Treaty of Küçük Kaynarca
events.description: After defeat by Russia, Ottomans signed humiliating Treaty of Küçük Kaynarca. Russia gained rights to protect Ottoman Orthodox Christians, becoming excuse for future interventions. Crimea became independent (later annexed by Russia).

events.title: Destruction of Janissaries
events.description: Sultan Mahmud II abolished conservative Janissary corps, which had become obstacle to modernization. Thousands of Janissaries were killed in 'Auspicious Incident'. This allowed Mahmud to establish modern army.

events.title: Tanzimat Reforms
events.description: Ottoman Empire implemented Tanzimat (Reorganization) reforms, attempting to modernize state and society. Reforms promoted equality for all subjects regardless of religion, modern education and legal systems. But reforms met resistance from conservatives.

events.title: Crimean War
events.description: Ottomans allied with Britain and France against Russia in Crimean War. Though victorious, war exposed Ottoman weakness. Congress of Paris temporarily preserved Ottoman territorial integrity.

events.title: First Constitutional Era
events.description: Under Young Ottoman pressure, Sultan Abdülhamid II promulgated Ottoman Constitution, establishing parliament. But Abdülhamid suspended constitution and parliament in 1878, establishing autocratic rule.

events.title: Treaty of Berlin
events.description: After Russo-Turkish War, Treaty of Berlin granted independence to Romania, Serbia and Montenegro. Bosnia-Herzegovina came under Austro-Hungarian administration. Ottoman Empire lost most European territory.

events.title: Young Turk Revolution
events.description: Committee of Union and Progress (Young Turks) forced Sultan Abdülhamid II to restore constitution. This Second Constitutional Era brought hopes of reform. But political instability and nationalism intensified.

events.title: Balkan Wars
events.description: Balkan League (Serbia, Bulgaria, Greece, Montenegro) attacked Ottoman Empire, capturing most remaining European territory. Ottomans lost nearly all Balkan possessions. Balkans' ethnic cleansing caused massive Muslim refugee flows to Anatolia.

events.title: World War I
events.description: Ottomans allied with Central Powers, fighting on multiple fronts. Empire suffered major defeats at Gallipoli (victory), Caucasus, Palestine and Mesopotamia. War devastated empire economy and population.

events.title: Armenian Genocide
events.description: Ottoman government systematically deported and massacred Armenian population. Estimates suggest 800,000 to 1.5 million Armenians died. This genocide remains highly controversial topic in Turkish politics. International community widely recognizes it as genocide.

events.title: Greek Occupation of Smyrna
events.description: With Allied support, Greece occupied Smyrna (Izmir) and western Anatolia, attempting to realize 'Greater Greece' dream. This sparked Turkish resistance. Mustafa Kemal led national liberation movement.

events.title: Turkish War of Independence
events.description: Under Mustafa Kemal's leadership, Turkish nationalists resisted Allied partition of Anatolia. Turkish army defeated Greek forces, expelling foreign occupiers. War established modern Turkey's borders.

events.title: Treaty of Sèvres
events.description: Allies imposed harsh Treaty of Sèvres on Ottoman Empire, partitioning Anatolia. But Turkish nationalists rejected treaty, continuing armed resistance. Treaty was never implemented.

events.title: Abolition of Sultanate
events.description: Grand National Assembly abolished Ottoman Sultanate, last Sultan Mehmed VI fled into exile. Over 600 years of Ottoman dynasty ended. Turkish Republic's foundation was laid.

events.title: Treaty of Lausanne
events.description: Turkey signed Treaty of Lausanne with Allies, replacing Treaty of Sèvres. Treaty recognized modern Turkey's borders and sovereignty. Greece and Turkey exchanged populations. This treaty is foundation of modern Turkish state.

events.title: Republic of Turkey Founded
events.description: The Grand National Assembly proclaimed the Republic of Turkey, Atatürk elected first president, Ankara the capital. This marked modern Turkey's birth. Atatürk began comprehensive modernization reforms.

events.title: Abolition of Caliphate
events.description: Grand National Assembly abolished Caliphate and exiled Ottoman dynasty. This severed Turkey's ties to Islamic past. Atatürk emphasized nationalism over Islamic identity.

events.title: Atatürk's Reforms
events.description: Atatürk implemented radical secularization and Westernization reforms: adopting Latin alphabet replacing Arabic script, banning fez, granting women suffrage, adopting Gregorian calendar and metric system, banning Sufi orders, establishing secular education system. These reforms fundamentally transformed Turkish society.

events.title: Death of Atatürk
events.description: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk died of cirrhosis aged 57. The nation mourned the father of the nation. His deputy İnönü succeeded as president, continuing Kemalist policies.

events.title: First Multi-Party Elections
events.description: Turkey held first free multi-party elections, Democrat Party defeated CHP. This marked transition to democratic politics. But military remained guardian of Kemalist secularism.

events.title: Turkey Joins NATO
events.description: Turkey joined NATO, firmly aligning with Western bloc in Cold War. Turkey became important NATO ally on Soviet southern flank. This shaped Turkey's geopolitical orientation for decades.

events.title: First Military Coup
events.description: Military overthrew elected government, executing Prime Minister Menderes and other leaders. This established pattern of military intervention in Turkish politics. Military claimed to protect secularism and Kemalism.

events.title: Military Memorandum
events.description: Military issued memorandum forcing government resignation, intervening in politics again. Turkey entered period of political instability and left-right violence.

events.title: Cyprus Intervention
events.description: After Greek-backed coup in Cyprus, Turkey invaded northern Cyprus to protect Turkish Cypriots. Turkey established Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus (TRNC), recognized only by Turkey. Cyprus issue remains unresolved conflict.

events.title: Military Coup of 1980
events.description: Amid civil unrest and terrorism, military staged coup, dissolving parliament and banning political parties. Thousands were arrested. Military rule lasted until 1983 elections. 1982 constitution increased military power.

events.title: PKK Insurgency Begins
events.description: Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) launched armed insurgency for Kurdish autonomy. Conflict killed over 40,000 people. Kurdish issue became Turkey's most serious internal challenge.

events.title: Application to EU
events.description: Turkey formally applied for European Economic Community (later EU) membership. This began Turkey's long EU accession process, still ongoing. EU membership became divisive issue in Turkish politics.

events.title: Tansu Çiller Becomes Prime Minister
events.description: Tansu Çiller became Turkey's first female prime minister. But her tenure was marked by corruption scandals and intensified Kurdish conflict.

events.title: Post-Modern Coup
events.description: Military forced out Islamist Prime Minister Erbakan in 'soft coup' without tanks. This demonstrated military's continued political power. Secularists saw it as necessary, Islamists as undemocratic intervention.

events.title: Capture of Öcalan
events.description: PKK leader Abdullah Öcalan was captured in Kenya, brought to Turkey for trial. He was sentenced to death (later commuted to life imprisonment). This was major blow to PKK.

events.title: İzmit Earthquake
events.description: Magnitude 7.6 earthquake struck İzmit region, killing over 17,000 people. Government's inadequate response exposed corruption and incompetence. Disaster damaged ruling parties' credibility.

events.title: Economic Crisis
events.description: Turkey suffered severe economic crisis, lira collapsed. IMF provided massive bailout. Crisis caused political realignment, paving way for AKP's rise.

events.title: AKP Comes to Power
events.description: Erdoğan's Islamist-conservative Justice and Development Party (AKP) won elections decisively. Erdoğan (due to prior conviction ineligible to run) first appointed Gül as PM, becoming PM himself in 2003. AKP promised economic development and EU reforms.

events.title: Economic Boom Years
events.description: Under AKP, Turkey experienced rapid economic growth, GDP tripled. Infrastructure modernized, poverty declined. But growth was debt-fueled and unequal. Erdoğan's popularity soared.

events.title: EU Accession Negotiations Begin
events.description: Turkey formally began EU accession negotiations. But talks stalled over Cyprus issue, human rights concerns and European skepticism. EU membership remains distant goal.

events.title: Headscarf Crisis and Constitutional Reform
events.description: AKP's attempt to elect Abdullah Gül as president sparked crisis with secularists. Military threatened intervention. But AKP won referendum and elections. This marked shift of power from military to AKP.

events.title: Constitutional Referendum
events.description: AKP's constitutional reforms passed in referendum, reducing military's political power. Reforms were popular but also increased executive power. This marked final defeat of military guardianship.

events.title: Gezi Park Protests
events.description: Protests against redevelopment of Istanbul's Gezi Park exploded into nationwide anti-government demonstrations. Erdoğan's harsh crackdown killed several protesters. Protests marked turning point, revealing deep societal divisions.

events.title: Kurdish Peace Process Collapse
events.description: Peace talks between government and PKK collapsed in 2015. Urban warfare in Kurdish southeast killed thousands. Government crackdown on Kurdish politicians and activists intensified conflict.

events.title: Erdoğan Elected President
events.description: Erdoğan elected Turkey's first directly-elected president. Though presidency was supposed to be ceremonial, Erdoğan continued to dominate politics. He began building 'New Turkey' with himself at center.

events.title: Failed Coup Attempt
events.description: A military faction attempted to overthrow Erdoğan's government but failed within hours. Erdoğan blamed the Gülen movement exiled in the US for orchestrating the coup. Post-coup, Erdoğan conducted massive purges, arresting tens of thousands, closing media and schools, consolidating personal power.

events.title: Constitutional Referendum
events.description: Turkey passed constitutional amendments via referendum (51.4% yes), changing from parliamentary to presidential system, vastly expanding presidential powers. Opposition alleged fraud. The new system took effect in 2018, Erdoğan became executive president, concentrating executive, legislative, judicial powers.

events.title: Syrian Interventions
events.description: Turkey launched multiple military operations in northern Syria (Olive Branch, Euphrates Shield, Peace Spring) to combat Kurdish YPG forces and create buffer zone. Operations displaced thousands, drew international criticism.

events.title: Economic Crisis
events.description: Turkish lira collapsed, losing 40% of its value against dollar. US sanctions over detained American pastor exacerbated crisis. High inflation and unemployment damaged Erdoğan's economic credibility.

events.title: Istanbul Election Re-run
events.description: After AKP lost Istanbul mayoral election, government annulled results and ordered re-vote. But opposition candidate Ekrem İmamoğlu won again by larger margin. Defeat in Turkey's largest city was major blow to Erdoğan.

events.title: Hagia Sophia Converted to Mosque
events.description: Erdoğan controversially converted Hagia Sophia from museum back to mosque, reversing Atatürk's 1935 secularization. This symbolized Turkey's turn toward Islamism and drew international criticism. UNESCO expressed concern about world heritage site.

events.title: Disputes with Greece and EU
events.description: Turkey's gas exploration in disputed Eastern Mediterranean waters escalated tensions with Greece and EU. Naval confrontations risked conflict. Turkey's assertive foreign policy alienated Western allies.

events.title: Major Earthquake Disaster
events.description: Southeastern Turkey and northern Syria suffered a 7.8 magnitude earthquake, causing over 50,000 deaths and millions homeless. Slow government response drew criticism. The earthquake exacerbated Turkey's economic and political crises.

events.title: Sweden NATO Accession Dispute
events.description: Turkey delayed Sweden's NATO membership for over a year, demanding extradition of alleged Kurdish militants. This demonstrated Turkey's ability to leverage NATO position. Turkey finally approved in 2024 after concessions.

events.title: Erdoğan Re-elected
events.description: In a fiercely contested presidential election, Erdoğan defeated opposition alliance candidate Kılıçdaroğlu with 52% of votes, winning a third presidential term. Erdoğan extended his rule beyond 20 years, becoming Turkey's longest-serving leader since Atatürk.

events.title: Ongoing Economic Challenges
events.description: Turkey continues facing high inflation (over 60%), weak lira and economic uncertainty. Erdoğan finally appointed orthodox economist as finance minister, implementing austerity measures to stabilize economy. Earthquake reconstruction and refugee burden exacerbate economic strain.
